report.math_notes: Verification of the k=24 / k=30 argument (the part actually written), which I find mathematically correct as a conditional theorem and recommend be declared as a new claim, e.g. 'cond_24_30: for k∈{24,30}, if S(s) holds for all 2≤s<k then S(k) holds'. Checks: Lemma 1 (normalisation m_i' = lcm of gcds, m_i' | L_k, gcds preserved, disjointness preserved via (*)) — correct. Lemma 3 (dividing by a common prime power q with common residue b: valuations give gcd(m_i/q,m_j/q)=g_ij/q, and g_ij/q ∤ (a_i−a_j)/q iff g_ij ∤ a_i−a_j) — correct. Lemma 4: needs q ≤ k−1 (from q | L_k), giving s=⌊(k−1)/q⌋+1 ∈ [2,k−1]; s<k since (k−1)/2+1<k for k≥2 — correct; the largest s invoked is ⌊(k−1)/2⌋+1 (12 for k=24, 15 for k=30), within the stated hypothesis. Corollary 5: ⌈k/p⌉ > ⌊(k−1)/p⌋ — correct. Lemma 6 uses only S(k−1) — correct. Step 4a: v_p(m_i)=1 since p²>k−1; g_ij=p for i≠j in J; P_i nonempty (Cor. 5), pairwise disjoint, ⊂ R — correct. Step 4b: ω well defined; injectivity since ℓ≥3 distinct common primes give g ≥ 30 ≥ k (for k=30, g ≥ 30 > 29) — correct. Step 4c: max product of ℓ positive integers with sum ≤ |R|: k=24 (|R|=8): 18,16,8,4,2,1 vs 21,20,19,18,17,16 — all excluded; k=30 (|R|=9): ℓ=4..9 give 24,16,8,4,2,1 vs 26..21 — excluded; ℓ=3 forces |P_j|=3 each, partition of R, ω bijective — correct (AM–GM equality case is genuinely forced since 27 ≤ ∏ ≤ 27). Step 4d: two triples differing only in the j''-coordinate are hit by distinct i_1,i_2 ∉ J, so rr' | g_{i_1 i_2} ≤ 29; the seven primes 5,…,23 pairwise have product ≥35>29 so all lie in one P_j of size 3 — contradiction, correct. The AM–GM text bounds are loose but valid; the brute-force table (trusted observation) is not needed for the proof. Dependency exposure: the result is conditional on S(s) for all s<k, which the cell permits provided stated (it is stated). The reported gap in O'Bryant's item 8 is not part of the verdict.
